chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān, from Ibn Abī ʿImrān al-Armanī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥakam, who said:

I asked him about four men who were drinking in a house, then two were killed and two were wounded. He said: “The two wounded ones are to be given the hadd punishment for wine, and they are to pay the value of the two slain ones. Their wounds are to be assessed, and compensation for them is to be returned to them from what they paid of the diyah. But if they die, then nothing is due from them, and their blood is without compensation.”

key_terms.حَدَّ الْخَمْرِ: the prescribed hadd punishment for drinking wine
key_terms.قِيمَةَ الْمَقْتُولَيْنِ: the compensation value of the two slain persons
key_terms.هَدَرَتْ دِمَاؤُهُمْ: their blood is treated as without compensable claim

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a group drinking wine fight and some are killed while others are wounded?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a violent incident among a group drinking wine. It combines the hadd for khamr with liability for the deaths, while also accounting for the wounds of the surviving injured parties through adjustment of the diyah.
